newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cambodia's Ranarridh still in France - family member.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranarridh still in France - family member.

text.p: Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh is still in France and is due to meet an aide to President Jacques Chirac on Monday, a family member said.

There was no immediate way of verifying the report. Ranariddh associates in France said on Sunday the prince had left France and was on his way back to Cambodia, where forces loyal to his rival, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, appeared to be in control of Phnom Penh and its outskirts.

The family member told Reuters on Monday by telephone that the Chirac aide would meet Prince Ranariddh later in the day in the southern town of Aix-en-Provence day where he is staying at the home of one of his sons.
Elysee officials were unavailable for comment.

Forces loyal to Ranariddh abandoned overnight their Tang Krasang stronghold in the west of the city, according to a Cambodian military intelligence official. It was not immediately clear where Ranariddh's men had withdrawn to.
At least 12 people were killed and 50 wounded in the weekend's fighting on the streets of Phnom Penh.
